The fog was so thick it felt like breathing wet wool. Elias Thorne, keeper of the Blackwood Point Light, wiped the condensation from the brass lens with a rag that had long since lost its color. He was halfway through his third cup of cold coffee when the radio crackled.

It wasn’t the static of the storm. It was a voice, clear as a bell, cutting through the whiteout.

“Elias. Stop the rotation.”

Elias froze. The heavy iron wheel of the lighthouse groaned as he let go of the handle. The beam, a massive slice of yellow light, halted in mid-sweep, pointing directly out into the void.

“Who is this?” Elias shouted into the receiver, his voice trembling. “This is a restricted frequency.”

“It’s me,” the voice said. There was a strange, metallic echo to it, as if the speaker were miles away, or perhaps centuries. “It’s me, Elias. From tomorrow.”

Elias laughed, a dry, brittle sound. “Tomorrow? I’m alone up here, mate. The supply boat won’t come until Thursday.”
